title: A free period removes 98 percent of the extra-wave fit gain in 86 GJ 433 HARPS exposures
abstract: We compare one searched velocity wave with one searched wave plus a fixed 36.059-day wave in 86 GJ 433 HARPS RVBank version 02 exposures. In the main quadratic model, two waves reduce weighted squared error by 33.885 relative to the fixed-period model, but by only 0.571 relative to the searched one-wave model. Thus a free period removes 98.316 percent of the apparent extra gain. Six controls remove 89.3 to 98.8 percent. Both period searches are repeated in conditional residual sign tests. Main tail fractions are 0.7710, 0.6995 and 0.6720 for 1, 30 and 90 day groups. No tested setting gives clear support for two waves. A noiseless one-wave check shows how a fixed comparison period can produce an apparent extra residual. This is a model comparison in one instrument, not a physical source identification or a refutation of the published planet system. Correlated activity, prior selection, simple trends and absent new independent observations limit inference. Original code, aggregate results, source hashes and retrieval steps support reproduction.

display.caption: One-wave and two-wave period profiles in the main model, and conditional noise tail fractions for seven model choices. Both searches are repeated in each draw. These fractions depend on the stated noise rule.
